sections.h2: Where do you take a deed in Gratiot County?
sections.html:
The counter is inside the Gratiot County Courthouse at 214 E Center Street in Ithaca, and the phone is 989-875-5217. Weekday hours run from 8:00 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon. Special closures are announced on the department page, such as the late-morning closing of November 10, 2026.

This is a constitutional office, and its counter handles more than 200 kinds of paper. Seller-side examples include warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, land contracts and mortgage releases, and the shelves also hold powers of attorney and oil and gas leases. Filings stretch back to the 1800s. Anyone may inspect a recorded document during business hours. The same window takes passport applications until 3:30 p.m., after a call to confirm availability.

Staff do not draft paperwork or give legal answers, so the deed itself is a job for an attorney or a title agent. Free public terminals sit on the courthouse's lower level and in the Treasurer's office.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges in Gratiot County?
sections.html:
One $30 charge covers a document of any length. Cash, check or card all work. Transfer tax and a tax certificate are added where they apply, and the $30 base is set in MCL 600.2567.

Gratiot County recording and copy charges
ServiceFee
Record one deed, mortgage or instrument$30
Every added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Warranty deed or land contract tax certificate$5
Copy of a real estate record$1 per page
Certifying a copy$5 per document plus $1 per page
Name search of the real estate record$0.50 per year, minimum $5

Parcel research is priced through the Treasurer's side. Terminal printouts run $1 per page, phone lookups $3, and a written property tax and assessment report $5 per parcel. A new online account gets one free parcel lookup, and later searches on records with the same owner name stay free.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Gratiot County sale owe?
sections.html:
Think in $500 blocks, rounding the price up. Each block pays 55 cents to the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 to the state under MCL 207.525, for $4.30 a block.

Try a $140,000 sale. It holds 280 blocks, which means $1,050.00 for the state, $154.00 for the county and $1,204.00 altogether, apart from the $30 filing. Raise the price by a dollar and the count moves to 281 blocks. Show the whole price on the deed or attach a value affidavit.

  • County exemptions: MCL 207.505. State exemptions: MCL 207.526.
  • No state tax on a deed issued in a foreclosure or in lieu of one.
  • No state tax on a conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or grandchild.
  • No tax of either kind on a corrective quitclaim that confirms title already held.

sections.h2: When does tax in Gratiot County become the county's problem?
sections.html:
The county sends bills July 1 and December 1. A current tax is paid locally, at the township, city or village office, until the first of March next year, and from that day it is the Gratiot County Treasurer's to collect. Payoff amounts come by phone.

The county's published schedule shows how years stack up. Open balances turn delinquent that first March 1. They become forfeited one year later. They are foreclosed on the March 31 after that. For 2025 bills that means forfeiture on March 1, 2027 and foreclosure on March 31, 2028. The online foreclosure auction for 2026 ran through tax-sale.info on a date set for August 7.

  • Cards work for delinquent balances through Graphite, which bills 2.75% with a $1 floor and turns away American Express.
  • Neither the county nor a local treasurer answers for an escrow company that skipped a payment on a mortgaged home.
  • A class settlement over surplus auction proceeds, which Gratiot County joined, covered tax foreclosure sales between 2013 and 2020. Its claim deadline of July 16, 2026 has gone by.
  • Since December 24, 2025 the Postal Service stamps the day mail is processed instead of the day it was dropped off, which can make a last-day envelope late.

sections.h2: What certificate does Gratiot County require for a warranty deed?
sections.html:
A $5 tax certificate from the Treasurer's office goes with warranty deeds, deeds containing a warranty covenant, land contracts and assignments of land contracts with a warranty clause. In MCL 211.135 the treasurer vouches that the last five years are paid and that no tax liens or tax titles hang over the land.

A quitclaim without covenants skips the step. For anything else, request the certificate early in the closing window and ask what an unpaid year would cost, because the register waits for it.

sections.h2: What happens to a deed after Gratiot County records it?
sections.html:
Clerks screen each document against Michigan law first. A deed that clears is given the next number, stamped with the time, scanned whole and cross indexed, and its legal description plus buyer and seller are keyed into the search system. A title company later leans on that index to follow ownership.

Township and city offices, Equalization and the Treasurer each learn of a sale from this register and use it to prepare valuations for the next tax roll. After recording, any member of the public may read or copy the deed. The office suggests double-checking a document against recording requirements before submitting it.

sections.h2: Where is Gratiot County and who lives there?
sections.html:
The county lies in central Michigan and was organized in 1855, named for Captain Charles Gratiot. Ithaca is the seat, Alma is the largest city, and St. Louis is the third city. Ashley, Breckenridge and Perrinton are villages. US 127 runs through Alma, Ithaca and St. Louis, while M-46 and M-57 cross it east and west. Seven counties border it, including Isabella, Saginaw and Montcalm. The Gratiot-Isabella Regional Education Service District is based in Ithaca.

The county covers about 572 square miles, mostly farmland and small towns. The courthouse is a classical revival building listed on the National Register, and the 212.8 MW Gratiot County Wind Project, opened in June 2012, is the largest wind installation in Michigan.

Population has hovered near 42,000 since 2000 (42,285 then, 42,476 in 2010, 41,761 in 2020), and the 2025 estimate of 41,190 is 1.4% under the 2020 base. The median age in the 2020 census was 39.7. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a median home value of $147,500, 78.9% owner occupancy, household income of $63,556 and median rent of $834. A sale at the median value of $147,500 would owe $1,268.50 in combined transfer tax.

faqs.q: Is there a card option for delinquent tax in Gratiot County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer takes cards for delinquent taxes through Graphite, which adds 2.75% with a $1 minimum. American Express is not accepted, and online payments are processed in the morning and afternoon.

faqs.q: Will the Gratiot County register write my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office prepares nothing and answers no legal questions, so hire a lawyer or title agent. Before you submit, review the deed against the recording requirements so the clerks do not have to send it back.

faqs.q: When do Gratiot County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: July 1 and December 1. If one never shows up, call the township, city or village treasurer, because the tax is still owed. Current-year tax stays payable at that local office until March 1.
